name: macos-execution-profile
purpose: Defines the macOS-specific execution structure for running the agent platform as a local desktop app, from development launch through signed and notarized distribution.

reader_guide.summary: Use this profile before claiming that the platform can run on macOS, adding Tauri/Electron app code, launching local agent services from a desktop shell, or preparing a DMG/ZIP/PKG release.
how_to_read: Read execution_levels to distinguish local developer launch from public Gatekeeper-friendly distribution.
Read process_model to understand which process owns UI, platform agent execution, workspace data access, and optional CLI adapters.
Read bundle_and_distribution_targets before choosing DMG, ZIP, or PKG.
Read signing_notarization_requirements before any outside-App-Store distribution claim.
Read smoke_tests before calling a macOS build runnable or release-ready.
update_triggers: The macOS desktop shell framework changes.
Tauri, Electron, Wails, or native packaging dependencies are installed.
The app starts launching Python agents, local services, file watchers, or external CLIs.
Signing, hardened runtime, entitlements, notarization, stapling, update, or installer behavior changes.
A macOS smoke test, Gatekeeper test, or first-run test fails.

structure_rules.rule: A developer-local macOS run may be unsigned or ad-hoc signed, but a public outside-App-Store build must be Developer ID signed, hardened-runtime enabled, notarized, and preferably stapled.
structure_rules.reason: A developer-local internal build and a Gatekeeper-friendly public app have different trust requirements.

structure_rules.rule: The macOS .app bundle owns the user entry point, while agent-platform remains the Python-first local platform layer behind a documented service, sidecar, or command boundary.
structure_rules.reason: The user should launch one app, but platform internals must remain maintainable and testable.

structure_rules.rule: The macOS app must not scan arbitrary folders before the user selects or creates a workspace and sees what will be indexed or executed.
structure_rules.reason: Installable software needs a stronger privacy boundary than a repository-local script.

structure_rules.rule: Missing Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub CLI, package managers, or deployment CLIs must disable only the related capability and show setup guidance.
structure_rules.reason: The macOS app should open and show useful history/agents even before every optional CLI is configured.

structure_rules.rule: Auto-update is not enabled until update artifacts, manifests, signatures, rollback behavior, and failure recovery are documented and smoke-tested.
structure_rules.reason: A broken update path can make local automation software harder to trust than manual workflows.

execution_levels.label: Developer local run
execution_levels.meaning: Run the UI and platform from the repository on the developer's Mac.
allowed_artifacts: future unsigned or ad-hoc signed Tauri/Electron app

execution_levels.label: Internal test app
execution_levels.meaning: A packaged .app used for local or trusted internal testing.
allowed_artifacts: dmg or zip for internal testers

execution_levels.label: Public outside-App-Store distribution
execution_levels.meaning: A normal user can download, open, update, and uninstall the app without Gatekeeper workarounds.
allowed_artifacts: signed pkg only if installer semantics are required

process_model.recommended_initial_shape: Tauri-first macOS .app shell wrapping workspace-monitor output, with agent-platform invoked through a documented local service or sidecar only after the service boundary is specified.
process_model.ui_process: Desktop shell presents workspace-monitor as the first UI and adds native dialogs only where macOS file/workspace selection or permissions need native behavior.
process_model.agent_process: Python agent-platform remains outside renderer code. It is launched later as a sidecar, local service, or explicit command boundary with lifecycle cleanup and logs.
process_model.data_process: Repository documents and generated snapshots are read only from user-selected workspace paths.
process_model.cli_process: External CLIs run only through adapter contracts with allowlisted commands, timeouts, output redaction, and capability_missing fallback.
process_model.background_process_policy: No file watcher, local daemon, or queue starts silently before the user selects a workspace and the app records lifecycle cleanup.

owns: dashboard, history, docs, agents, source viewer, and decision inbox UI surfaces
research, planning, evaluation, config checks, and governance validators
tool-specific command invocation under explicit adapter contracts

bundle_and_distribution_targets.purpose: Native macOS application bundle for local launch and as the unit inside DMG/ZIP.
Primary outside-App-Store installer-like distribution candidate for normal macOS users.
Useful for update feeds or simple archive distribution when tooling requires it.
Use only when installer scripts, privileged installation, or managed deployment semantics are truly required.

signing_notarization_requirements.entitlement_policy: Start with no extra entitlements; add only those required by measured macOS behavior, such as workspace file access or update behavior.
signing_notarization_requirements.secret_policy: Apple credentials, signing identities, API keys, and update private keys must be injected through local keychain, CI secrets, or environment variables; they must not be committed.
signing_notarization_requirements.ad_hoc_signing_policy: Ad-hoc signing is acceptable only for developer-local or trusted internal builds and must not be described as public distribution-ready.

permissions_entitlements.notes: Use native folder picker or explicit workspace path. Do not scan home directories by default.
Needed only for update checks, web research, notifications, or remote services; document endpoint class before release.
All CLI execution must go through adapter contracts and visible user consent.
Slack, Discord, Teams, and OS notifications remain optional capabilities.

update_strategy.tauri_path: Use Tauri updater only after update server or static manifest hosting, update signing keys, rollback policy, and failure UI are documented.
update_strategy.electron_fallback_path: Use Electron autoUpdater or electron-builder only after signing, ZIP/update feed requirements, and rollback behavior are tested.
update_strategy.manual_update_fallback: Before auto-update, provide versioned downloads and explicit migration notes.

smoke_tests.check: Open local UI from a selected workspace and verify history, docs, agent catalog, and source viewer render.
Install/open the app on a clean macOS account without developer repository state.
Confirm the app asks for a workspace before indexing or running commands.
Remove or hide optional CLIs and verify only related capabilities are disabled.
Download the notarized artifact on a separate Mac or clean VM, open it normally, and verify no Gatekeeper workaround is required.
Simulate update unavailable, bad manifest, and rollback paths before enabling auto-update.

release_gates: Framework decision record comparing Tauri, Electron, and native packaging remains current.
Project-local dependency installation audit exists if desktop dependencies are installed.
macOS app process model and sidecar/local-service lifecycle are documented.
Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, entitlements, notarization, and stapling plan is complete.
No secrets or private repository snapshots are bundled.
Workspace boundary and optional CLI degradation smoke tests pass.
Update, rollback, uninstall, and failure recovery are documented and tested before public release.

planned_commands.command: To be decided after Tauri dependency installation audit; likely a project-local Tauri dev command wrapping workspace-monitor output.
To be decided after signing and notarization strategy; public distribution command must inject signing credentials securely.
